gaps.concept: MEN1 and MEN2 are autosomal dominant; MEN1 tumors follow a two-hit tumor-suppressor mechanism, whereas RET encodes an activated receptor tyrosine kinase.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes the inheritance and cancer mechanisms in a family with multiple endocrine tumors.

gaps.concept: Primary hyperparathyroidism is usually the earliest MEN1 manifestation; elevated calcium with elevated PTH commonly reflects multigland disease.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies MEN1 in a young patient with hypercalcemia before other tumors become apparent.

gaps.concept: Prolactinoma is the most common pituitary tumor in MEN1.
gaps.why_tested: Links galactorrhea, amenorrhea, or hypogonadism to a familial endocrine tumor syndrome.

gaps.concept: MEN2B usually lacks the parathyroid disease seen in MEN2A.
gaps.why_tested: Separates the two MEN2 syndromes when thyroid and adrenal tumors coexist.

gaps.concept: Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from calcitonin-secreting C cells and contains stromal amyloid derived from calcitonin.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the thyroid tumor from elevated calcitonin or Congo red-positive stroma.

gaps.concept: MEN2-associated medullary thyroid carcinoma often arises from C-cell hyperplasia and is multifocal or bilateral.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes inherited medullary thyroid carcinoma from a sporadic solitary lesion.

gaps.concept: Pheochromocytomas arise from neural crest-derived adrenal medullary chromaffin cells and secrete catecholamines.
gaps.why_tested: Connects adrenal tumor origin to episodic sympathetic symptoms.

gaps.concept: Pheochromocytoma classically causes episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes a catecholamine-secreting tumor from a characteristic symptom cluster.

gaps.concept: Pheochromocytoma is detected by elevated plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines.
gaps.why_tested: Selects the biochemical finding in a patient with episodic hypertension or MEN2.

gaps.concept: Pheochromocytoma shows vascular nests of chromaffin cells in a Zellballen pattern.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the tumor from an adrenal histology image.

gaps.concept: Alpha blockade precedes beta blockade in pheochromocytoma; beta blockade first can provoke unopposed alpha-mediated hypertensive crisis.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the consequence of starting a beta blocker in a catecholamine-secreting tumor.

gaps.concept: Hereditary pheochromocytomas may be bilateral; associated syndromes include MEN2, von Hippel–Lindau disease, and neurofibromatosis type 1.
gaps.why_tested: Links bilateral adrenal tumors or a syndromic family history to inherited pheochromocytoma.

gaps.concept: Loss of succinate dehydrogenase function predisposes to hereditary pheochromocytoma and extra-adrenal paraganglioma.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the genetic defect in a family with multiple catecholamine-producing tumors.

gaps.concept: Insulinoma causes fasting hypoglycemia with symptoms that resolve after glucose administration: Whipple triad.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes an insulin-secreting tumor in a patient with recurrent fasting confusion or diaphoresis.

gaps.concept: During insulinoma-induced hypoglycemia, insulin, C-peptide, and proinsulin remain inappropriately elevated; exogenous insulin suppresses C-peptide.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes endogenous insulin secretion from injected insulin in a hypoglycemia workup.

gaps.concept: Sulfonylurea exposure mimics insulinoma's insulin and C-peptide pattern; a drug screen distinguishes them.
gaps.why_tested: Resolves a hypoglycemia vignette when both insulin and C-peptide are elevated.

gaps.concept: Gastrinoma produces high fasting gastrin with low gastric pH; proton pump inhibitors or atrophic gastritis can raise gastrin without acid hypersecretion.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes Zollinger–Ellison syndrome from other causes of hypergastrinemia.

gaps.concept: Excess gastric acid in Zollinger–Ellison syndrome inactivates pancreatic enzymes, contributing to malabsorption and diarrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Explains diarrhea accompanying recurrent peptic ulcers.

gaps.concept: VIPoma causes secretory diarrhea that persists during fasting, with bicarbonate loss producing non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
gaps.why_tested: Separates VIPoma from osmotic diarrhea and predicts its acid–base pattern.

gaps.concept: Somatostatinoma suppresses insulin, cholecystokinin, and gastrin release, explaining diabetes, gallstones, and low gastric acid.
gaps.why_tested: Connects the tumor's hormone to its combination of metabolic and digestive findings.

gaps.concept: Serotonin-producing carcinoid tumors commonly originate from midgut enterochromaffin cells.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the likely primary tumor in a patient with carcinoid syndrome and liver metastases.

gaps.concept: Bronchial or ovarian carcinoids can cause carcinoid syndrome without liver metastases because their venous drainage bypasses portal circulation.
gaps.why_tested: Explains carcinoid symptoms when imaging shows no liver metastases.

gaps.concept: Carcinoid heart disease typically causes tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonic stenosis through fibrotic valve plaques; pulmonary serotonin inactivation usually spares left-sided valves.
gaps.why_tested: Predicts the specific valve lesions or explains predominantly right-sided findings.

gaps.concept: Carcinoid tumors may trigger acute flushing, bronchospasm, and hemodynamic instability during anesthesia or tumor manipulation.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies carcinoid crisis in a perioperative vignette.
